title: CLCON/321/2013 of Smt Mridula Singh Vs Dr. Akhilesh Kumar

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Contempt Petition No. 321 of 2013
Smt. Mridula Singh .....Applicant
Versus
Dr. Akhilesh Kumar and another ....Respondents
Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Devang Dobhal, Advocate for the
respondent.

Dated: 13th December, 2018
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.

The precise fact which has been pleaded by the
petitioner, applicant herein, in the writ petition were that the
Campus School of G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and
Technology, Pant Nagar, District Udham Singh Nagar has issued
an advertisement on 25th January, 1984 for the purposes of
appointment of Primary School Teachers in the aforesaid
Institution, being run and managed by the said University. The
petitioner, after undergoing the process of selection was
substantively appointed on 20th June, 1988, and, according to her,
she claims to have an unblemished service record till she has
attained the age of superannuation on 28th February, 2011. She
contends that after having attained the age of superannuation, she
has moved an application on 27th January, 2011, before the
respondents, stating therein that as per the service tenor rendered
by her, she would be entitled for a payment of gratuity to her to the
tune of Rs.3,26,719/- which was required to be re-calculated based
on the enhancement payable to her on account of implementation
of the new grade pay. When the same was not remitted, the
petitioner submitted her claim by way of submitting a
representations on 14th March, 2011 and 11th October, 2011 and,
ultimately, when all the efforts made by the petitioner failed and

2
lastly she submitted the representation on 24th of December, 2011,
according to her, calculation of the amount of gratuity payable to
her ought to have been increased upto a total amount of
Rs.4,16,124/-. Claiming the said amount, the petitioner has filed
Writ Petition, being Writ Petition (S/S) No. 816 of 2012, wherein
she has sought for the following reliefs :-
"A. To issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus commanding the respondents to forthwith release
the remaining amount of Gratuity to the petitioner.
B. To issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus commanding the Respondents to pay interest at
the delayed payment of Gratuity at a rate to be specified by
this Hon'ble Court.
C. To issue any other writ order or direction which
this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and necessary in the
circumstances of the case.
D. To award the cost of the writ petition in favour of
the petitioner."
2. After exchange of the pleadings, the writ petition
came for consideration before the learned Single Judge and the
same has been decided by the judgment dated 24th June, 2013.
Primarily, this Court in the contempt jurisdiction will be concerned
with regard to the interpretation and impact of the finding which
has been recorded by the learned Single Judge in para 9 of the said
judgment, which is quoted hereunder :-
"9. Although the petitioner claims that as per the
formula given in Section 4 (2) of the Payment of Gratuity
Act, 1972, the amount of gratuity would come to
Rs.4,16,124/- on the basis of last salary drawn by him as
Rs.26,717/-, the amount of gratuity actually passed in favour
of the petitioner by the formula devised by the respondent
the amount is Rs.89,044/-. This approach of the respondent
school is absolutely wrong. There is no doubt that the
petitioner is covered under the Payment of Gratuity Act and
therefore gratuity is liable to be calculated as per the
formula given in the said Act and not as per the formula
devised by the school. Writ petition is therefore succeeds.
Respondents are directed to calculate gratuity of the
petitioner as per section 4 (2) of the Payment of Gratuity Act
within a period of 6 weeks from the date a certified copy of
this order is produced 5 before the concerned authority. It is

3
however, made clear that the amount already paid to the
petitioner towards gratuity be adjusted."
3. After rendering of the judgment dated 24.06.2013, the
petitioner contends that for seeking its compliance, the petitioner
has moved an application before the respondent but despite of the
fact that the controversy stood settled with regard to the quantum
of gratuity and its mode of calculation by the judgment dated 24th
June, 2013, yet, the respondents have only paid only a meager
amount of gratuity to the tune of Rs. 98,825/- only in his favour.
4. Hence, the petitioner preferred the contempt petition
on 11th October, 2013, alleging non compliance of the judgment
dated 24th June, 2013.
5. This Court on initiation of the contempt proceedings
issued notices and after issuance of the notices, the respondents
have filed the counter affidavit, and on induction of new
incumbent in the office of the respondents, they were later on
impleaded as party respondents to the contempt petition,
ultimately, allowing of the last impleadment application which was
done by the Court by the order dated 16th April, 2015, when the
present Officer was impleaded.
6. The argument of the learned counsel for the petitioner
is from the view point that when an employee after attaining the
age of superannuation falls to be within the ambit of Payment of
Gratuity Act, in that eventuality, if the gratuity has to be
calculated, it has to be calculated in accordance with the formula as
contemplated under Section 4 of Sub-section (2) of the Act which
is quoted hereunder :
"4. Payment of gratuity -
(1).....
(2) For every completed year of service or part
thereof in excess of six months, the employer shall pay
gratuity to an employed at the rate of fifteen days' wages

4
based on the rate of wages last drawn by the employee
concerned:
Provided that in the case of a piece-rated employee,
daily wages shall be computed on the average of the total
wages received by him for a period of three months
immediately preceding the termination of his employment,
and, for this purpose, the wages paid for any overtime work
shall not be taken into account :
Provided further that in the case of [an employee who
is employed in a seasonal establishment and who is not so
employed throughout the year], the employer shall pay the
gratuity at the rate of seven days' wages for each season.
 [Explanation. - In the case of a monthly rated
employee, the fifteen days' wages shall be calculated by
dividing the monthly rate of wages last drawn by him by
twenty-six and multiplying the quotient by fifteen.]"
7. Argument of the learned counsel for the petitioner,
which was agitated before the learned Single Judge as well as
before this Court is to the effect that when a payment is due to be
made to an incumbent and, in particular, when it is to be done
under the statute, for example, in the instant case under Payment of
Gratuity Act, then its calculation ought to be made strictly in
accordance with the formula laid down under the said Act itself
and no other principle or formula could be adopted other than the
one which is specified under the Act for the purposes of
determining the gratuity payable to the employee.
8. His submission is that in view of the observation
which has been made by the learned Single Judge, the learned
Single Judge has denounced the adoption of the formula devised
by the School for calculation of the gratuity.
 9. In response to the contempt petition, counter affidavit
has been filed by the respondent and the learned counsel for the
respondent has harped upon the reply in particular the reply which
has been extended in para 14 of the counter affidavit, wherein the
respondents has pleaded that in compliance of the judgment passed
by this Court, the calculation of the gratuity has been strictly done

5
in accordance with the formula contemplated under Sub-section (2)
of Section 4 of the Act, and accordingly, after the calculation, the
amount arrived was Rs.1,87,869/- has been determined to be
payable to the petitioner.
10. He further in support of his argument submits that the
formula as adopted for making the payment of gratuity by invoking
Section 4 (2) of the Act, as a matter of fact, has had to be in
consonance to the amendment made in the Act by virtue of the
Amending Act No. 47 of 2009, as made effective from 31st
December, 2009, wherein, for the first time in the definition of the
employee given in 2 (e) of the Act, as it had been amended had
included the teachers' of the private schools too to be falling
within the ambit of definition of an employee and, hence, the
submission is that on the date of the retirement for calculation of
the gratuity, it has been rightfully done by invocation of Section 4
(2) of the Act, the fact which stood denied by the petitioner.
11. Reverting back to the interpretation of the direction
issue by the learned Single Judge and it compliance, this Court in
exercise of its contempt jurisdiction has to scrutinize as to what
was actually directed by Single Judge which was required to be
complied with. The judgment dated 24th June, 2013 has
specifically mentioned that the formula, which was to be adopted
for calculation would be the statutory formula provided under
Section 4 (2) of the Act and no other formula as devised by the
Institution would be applicable for calculating the gratuity, which
is a benefit payable under an Act.
12. The learned counsel for the respondents harped upon
the pleading of para 14 of the counter affidavit, wherein, specific
plea has been taken by them by making reference to the formula
adopted for calculation of the gratuity in case of petitioner and
contends that as a matter of fact whatever claim has been derived

6
and paid to the petitioner was strictly in compliance of the
direction issued by this Court on 24th June, 2013.
13. This Court, while appreciating the pleading of para
14 of the counter affidavit has considered the same and looking to
the pleadings raised in para 14 rather it reflects that the
respondents have adopted the formula given under Sub-section (2)
of Section 4 of the Act. If there is any variation in the
computation in the amount payable by way of gratuity and the
petitioner is dissatisfied, then it is always a subject matter of
challenge in an independent proceedings but inappropriate
mathematical calculations, its adequacy cannot be said to be falling
within ambit of the judgment dated 24th June, 2013 and if at all the
petitioner was dissatisfied by the mode of calculation or the
wrongful calculation or inadequacy of amount calculated, it will
not be a contempt because at least the order has been complied
with.
14. Thus, this Court does not find any merit in the
contempt petition and the same is accordingly dismissed.
